standard.description: Measuring Receiver (RF power, tuned RF level, AM / FM / PM, frequency, audio, carrier noise options)
standard.reference: HP 8902A Measuring Receiver manual (PDF title "8902A Measuring Receiver Quick Reference Guide"), Section I General Information, Table 1-1 Specifications (1 of 7 ... 7 of 7), printed pp.1-20 to 1-26 (PDF pp.46-53); "page" fields in this file are PDF page numbers (1-20 = 46, 1-21 = 47, 1-22 = 48, 1-23 = 49, 1-24 = 50, 1-24.1 = 51, 1-25 = 52, 1-26 = 53)
standard.author: built from the manual page images by specs/build_8902a_standard_from_manual.py

notes.1: p.1-20 footnote 1: not to exceed for the stated accuracy: 50 Hz to 40 kHz rates with the rms detector.
notes.2: p.1-20 footnote 2: peak residuals must be accounted for in peak readings.
notes.3: p.1-20 footnote 3: for peak measurements only, AM accuracy may be affected by distortion generated by the measuring receiver; in the worst case this can decrease accuracy by 0.1 % of reading for each 0.1 % of distortion.
notes.4: p.1-20 footnote 4: flatness is the variation in indicated AM depth for constant depth on the input signal.
notes.5: p.1-20 footnote 5: for optimum flatness, cables should be terminated with their characteristic impedance.
notes.6: p.1-20 footnote 6: but not to exceed 20 kHz rates and 40 kHz peak deviations with the 750 us de-emphasis filter.
notes.7: p.1-20 footnote 7: with 750 us de-emphasis and pre-display "off", distortion is not specified for modulation outputs >4 V peak (can occur near maximum deviation for a measurement range, at rates <2 kHz).
notes.9: p.1-22 footnote 9: the fundamental RF Power measurement units are watts; all other units are derived from that number.
notes.10: p.1-22 footnote 10: with the HP 8484A sensor the noise specification may mask the linearity specification; on the top RF power range add the sensor linearity percentages from the sensor specifications.
notes.11: p.1-22 footnote 11: the fundamental Tuned RF Level measurement units are volts; all other units are derived from that number.
notes.12: p.1-23 footnote 12: Tuned RF Level accuracy is affected by residual FM of the source under test; if residual FM(peak) is >50 Hz measured over 30 s in a 3 kHz BW, use the IF average detector (30 kHz BW) via Special Function 1.9 (sensitivity then -100 dBm).
notes.13: p.1-23 footnote 13: IF ranges 6 and 7 are used only in automatic operation, below about -110 dBm (IF synchronous detector) and below about -85 dBm (IF average detector).
notes.14: p.1-24.1 footnote 14: Option 050 specifications are warranted with an HP synthesized source with <100 Hz peak residual FM measured in a 3 kHz post-detection bandwidth over 30 s.
notes.15: p.1-24.1 footnote 15: accuracy specifications do not include mismatch uncertainty.
notes.16: p.1-25 footnote 16: with the audio low-pass and high-pass filters used to stabilize frequency readings.
notes.17: p.1-25 footnote 17: for demodulated signals the residual noise generated by the 8902A must be accounted for in distortion measurements (residual AM, FM or PhiM).
notes.18: p.1-25 footnote 18: the >20 kHz low-pass filter is intended for minimum overshoot with square wave modulation.
notes.19: p.1-26 footnote 19: external reference accuracy affects accuracy of all measurements.
notes.20: Storage: dB / dBm / dBc / dBc/Hz as printed; "% of reading" as a fraction in rel; dimensionless percent limits (THD, residual AM, ...) as a fraction in abs with unit "ratio" (0.1 % = 0.001); modulation depth as a fraction; deviations in Hz peak; PM in radians. Page fields are PDF pages (printed page 1-20 = PDF 46; see the standard header).
notes.21: Printed as "+/- N % of reading +/- 1 digit": only the percent of reading is stored. The "+/- 1 digit" term depends on the display resolution in use and has no field.
notes.22: Printed under the table: "For rms detector add +/-3 % of reading". NOT added to the stored value (the manual does not say whether the terms add linearly); apply it by hand when the rms detector is used.
notes.23: Spec limit with no period printed: stored with the period label "spec" (the manual gives no calibration interval for Table 1-1). Pass period="spec" to lookup().
notes.24: Supplemental Characteristic (printed in italics): typical, not warranted. Period label "supplemental".
notes.25: Modulation rows: amp band = the printed Deviations / Depths column (lower bound 0 where only "<=" or "to" is printed), freq band = the printed carrier "Frequency Range", the printed modulation Rates are the qualifier tagged "rate".
notes.26: Limit printed as "<" (upper bound, not a +/- tolerance): stored with le = true.
notes.27: Option required: Carrier Noise = Options 030-037; Increased Power Measurement Accuracy = Option 050; 1E-9/day time base = Option 002.
notes.28: RF Power rows: amp band = the printed RF range with the HP 11722A Sensor Module (range 1 -20 to -10 dBm ... range 5 +20 to +30 dBm, p.1-22); the frequency band 100 kHz to 2.6 GHz is the 11722A range printed in the section introduction, not repeated on the limit lines.
notes.29: RF Power: the limit is stated "using Recorder Output"; using the front-panel display add +/-1 count of the least-significant digit (not stored).

problems.what: Direction is "input" (the 8902A measures). specmanager.StandardSpec.lookup() defaults to direction="output" and period "1 yr": pass direction="input" (or None) and period="spec" (or "supplemental") to find these rows. Rows are kind OTHER (variant names the quantity) except FREQ (audio counter) and ACV (audio rms level).
Confidence level / coverage factor is NOT stated in Table 1-1 (confidence_pct left empty). The manual gives no calibration period for the specifications either (period label "spec").

Units stored as printed (dBm, dBc, dBc/Hz, dB, dB/dB, dB/10dB, dB/range, dB/kHz, ratio, rad): the schema has no log-unit conversion and no unit validation for them. A "ratio" value of 0.001 is 0.1 %. Fixed dB terms are NOT combinable with a relative (rel) term by the generic spec_value() arithmetic: they are not linear quantities.

problems.where: Modulation / Frequency Modulation, Amplitude Modulation, Phase Modulation accuracy
problems.what: Every accuracy is printed "+/-N % of reading +/- 1 digit": the "+/- 1 digit" term (resolution dependent) is not stored, and "For rms detector add +/-3 % of reading" is not applied (pp.1-20, 1-21). Footnote 1 limits the stated accuracy to 50 Hz to 40 kHz rates with the rms detector.

The four printed rows overlap (e.g. 150 kHz-10 MHz, 50 Hz-10 kHz, 5 %-99 % is inside 20 Hz-10 kHz, to 99 %); a lookup by carrier frequency alone matches two rows. "to 99 %" depth has no printed lower bound: stored from 0. Choose by rate and depth by hand.

No deviation limits are printed for PM accuracy in the table (only a rate-vs-deviation graph on p.1-21, not read): amp band left empty, so lookup() skips these rows. Rates, carrier ranges and percentages are stored.

Printed as "<8 Hz rms at 1300 MHz, decreasing linearly with frequency to <1 Hz rms for 100 MHz and below": a frequency-dependent limit the schema cannot hold. Stored as two rows (<1 Hz up to 100 MHz; <8 Hz as the upper bound for 100 MHz to 1300 MHz); the first row starts at 150 kHz (the RF Input range, p.1-26) because the table says only "100 MHz and below".

Rows with "rates 400 Hz or 1 kHz" use two discrete qualifiers (400 Hz and 1 kHz), not a range. AM rejection / FM rejection / residual AM / AM and PM distortion limits are upper bounds ("<", le = true), not +/- tolerances. Rows whose carrier range is not printed (AM distortion, residual AM, PM distortion) have no frequency band.

NOT STORED: AM calibrator depth 33.33 % nominal "internally calibrated to an accuracy of +/-0.1 %" and FM calibrator deviation 34 kHz peak nominal "+/-0.1 %": the manual does not say whether +/-0.1 % is of the value or absolute depth/percent. Supplemental carrier 10.1 MHz, rate 10 kHz, level -25 dBm are nominal values (not tolerances).

NOT STORED: accuracy "+/- reference accuracy +/-3 counts of least-significant digit" (fc < 100 MHz) and "+/- reference accuracy +/-3 counts of least-significant digit or 30 Hz, whichever is larger" (fc >= 100 MHz). A count-based limit depends on the resolution in use (maximum resolution 1 Hz); the schema has no counts or max() term. Range 150 kHz to 1300 MHz, sensitivity (12 mV rms / -25 dBm, 150 kHz-650 MHz; 22 mV rms / -20 dBm, 650-1300 MHz) and manual-tuning sensitivity 0.22 mV rms (-60 dBm) are minimum-level figures, not tolerances. Time base reference accuracy is stored separately (aging rows).

The two ">1 kHz" lines (+/-3 counts of least-significant digit, demodulated and external) are NOT stored (count-based). Stored fixed terms (+/-0.02 Hz, +/-0.2 Hz) exclude the "+/- internal reference accuracy" term printed with each; the frequency band is stored in the amp slot (kind FREQ). Printed modulation conditions are stored as qualifiers (lower limits only for ">="); row 3 lower and upper limits come from the printed "1.5 % <= AM < 10 %" etc. External signal row: frequency printed "<1 kHz" (not "<=").

ZERO SET (+/-0.5 % +/-1 count of full scale on lowest range) and the supplemental zero drift: "Decrease by a factor of 10 for each higher range" is ambiguous (the percentage or the resulting value); only the lowest range is stored. Full scale for range 1 (100 uW) is taken from the printed range 1 limit (-10 dBm). HP 8484A noise ("multiply noise by 5 on all ranges") and the front-panel "+/-1 count" are not stored.

NOT STORED: RF power resolution (0.01 % of full scale; 0.01 dB), "LINEARITY (includes sensor non-linearity): RF range linearity +/- RF range-to-range change error" (a sum of two stored terms), response times (<10 s / <1 s / <100 ms), cal-factor table sizes and limits, displayed units, and the sensor-module ranges are used only as amp bands. The frequency band 100 kHz-2.6 GHz comes from the section introduction (11722A); other 8480-series sensors cover -70 dBm to +44 dBm and 100 kHz to 50 GHz (manual text, not tabulated).

The 1.2 % worst case / 0.9 % rss figures are "for one year (0 C to 55 C)": stored with period "1 yr" and "1 yr (rss)". Factory setting +/-0.7 % stored with period "factory setting". 50 MHz is a supplemental "nominal" frequency (SWR 1.05 nominal, Type-N female not stored).

NOT STORED: "RELATIVE MEASUREMENT ACCURACY: detector linearity + IF range-to-range error + RF range-to-range error + frequency drift error + noise error +/-1 digit" (a recipe summing stored terms; no total is printed); the IF range plots and the two attenuator-test uncertainty graphs on p.1-23 (curves, not tables); power range -127 to 0 dBm / -100 to 0 dBm and frequency 2.5-1300 MHz are used as bands; displayed resolution; IF frequency 455 kHz; acquisition and response times (<4 s / <10 s; <2 s / <5 s); displayed units.

Detector linearity is two limits per row (per dB of change, and a cap per 10 dB): stored as two specs on one row (periods "spec" and "spec, per 10 dB"; units dB/dB and dB/10dB). IF average detector limit is "(0 C to +35 C)". The IF range-to-range rows have no level band (IF range boundaries are only in the plot, p.1-23); the IF range is a qualifier.

Noise error "+/-0.18 dB for levels <-120 dBm, or for levels <-110 dBm if Special Function 1.9 is selected": the lower bound -127 dBm is the Tuned RF power-range floor, not printed with the limit; the second row is therefore a reading of an ambiguous sentence (Special Function 1.9 selects the IF average detector, footnote 12, whose own range starts at -100 dBm). Verify against the printed text before use.
Input SWR limits are "<" (le = true), tagged by RF range number (qualifier "RF range"); there is no level band. The IF / RF range numbers are instrument ranges, not values.

Each limit is "+/-X dB/10 dB step +/-Y dB +/-1 digit": a fixed term and a per-10-dB-step term. Stored as two specs on one row ("spec" = fixed term in dB, "spec, per 10 dB step" = step term, unit dB/10dB); the combination as a function of the attenuation step (graph, p.1-24.1) cannot be expressed. "+/-1 digit" not stored. Mismatch uncertainty is excluded (footnote 15); only warranted with an HP synthesized source (footnote 14). The second band is printed "-100.001 dBm to -120.000 dBm".

Relative accuracy bands are printed as lower limits only (levels >= -95 dBc, >= -129 dBc/Hz): stored as qualifiers with lo = hi, no amp band. NOT STORED (minimum or nominal, not tolerances): carrier rejection >90 dB (temp <=35 C), dynamic range 115 dB, carrier noise filter noise bandwidth 2.5 kHz nominal, filter shapes (graphs), adjacent/alternate-channel filter bandwidths, typical noise floor -150 dBc/Hz.

NOT STORED: sensitivity thresholds (0.15 kHz peak FM, 1.5 % peak AM, 0.6 rad peak PhiM, 100 mV rms external), measurement bandwidth, maximum input 3 V rms, audio input impedance 100 kohm, frequency ranges 20 Hz-250 kHz (counter) and usable to 600 kHz, measurement rates, de-emphasis 3 dB frequencies (6366 / 3183 / 2122 / 212 Hz), filter pole counts. Audio distortion: "+/-1 dB of reading" is stored as a fixed dB term (abs = 1 dB); the fundamentals are 400 Hz +/-5 % and 1 kHz +/-5 % (stored as 380-420 Hz and 950-1050 Hz). Filter flatness rows have no frequency band (rates are stated as >= or <= only; the condition is in the label).

Stored under functions named "[Supplemental Characteristics]" or in rows with period "supplemental" / explicit non-spec periods: typical, NOT warranted. NOT STORED: stereo separation (50 Hz to 15 kHz) >47 dB and other minimum / "usable" figures (greater-than limits have no field: le only means "<="), FM / AM / PM maximum-resolution and demodulated-output-sensitivity tables, detectors, rear-panel input/output characteristics, general specifications (temperature 0-55 C, power, weight, EMI, HP-IB codes), RF Input operating level table (12 mV rms / -25 dBm and 22 mV rms / -20 dBm minimum, 7 V rms (1 W peak) maximum, source SWR <4, max safe DC 5 V).

The aging rows are fractions (1E-6 per month; 1E-9 per day, Option 002) with periods "1 month" / "1 day" and le = true; the manual says after a 30-day warm-up (footnote 8). Supplemental temperature, line-voltage and short-term-stability figures are stored with period "supplemental" (units per degC / per line change / 1 s average are in the variant text).

Read from rendered images (110 dpi; 170 dpi crops of pp.1-20, 1-22, 1-25). The footnote superscripts on headings were read from the 110/170 dpi images; a few (e.g. which footnote applies to which sub-table) are small print: verify the footnote attachments (params notes) against the page before relying on them.
The validator warning below about an overlapping range is expected: the two printed limits (<0.3 % for depth <=50 %, <0.6 % for depth <=95 %) are nested by design.
Confidence level is not specified on the sheet; set the coverage divisor in the manager before relying on this standard.
